question: Why do we actively monitor injection safety devices in the ward?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of bloodborne infections
options.B: To measure the speed of nursing staff during shifts
options.C: To track the monthly financial budget of the pharmacy
options.D: To calculate the total electricity consumed by equipment

explanation: Spot on! Tracking these tools ensures safety devices are used right, keeping both patients and us safe from nasty infections like HIV and hepatitis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: What makes needle-stick injuries so scary for us on the clinical floor?

options.A: They automatically disqualify a nurse from clinical duty
options.B: They cause immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: They can transmit serious bloodborne pathogens easily
options.D: They always lead to permanent nerve damage in the hand

explanation: Exactly. A used needle carries patient blood straight into your bloodstream, which is a major risk for infections. Always handle sharps with care! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the main goal of filling out that monthly injection safety monitoring form?

options.A: To schedule annual leave periods for the clinical team
options.B: To evaluate the bedside nursing skills of newly hired staff
options.C: To guarantee an uninterrupted supply of safety devices
options.D: To determine the salary scales for hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! The form helps us keep an eye on stock levels so our clinic never suddenly runs out of syringes and safety boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why do we track wastage rates on our monthly injection safety form?

options.A: It automatically increases the monthly government drug allocation
options.B: It helps managers justify future procurement requests and reduce loss
options.C: It replaces the need for keeping a physical pharmacy inventory
options.D: It punishes nurses who accidentally drop sterile items

explanation: Spot on! Tracking broken or wasted items shows management where supplies are leaking, helping us order better next time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which of these details is typically recorded in the stock inventory part of the safety form?

options.A: The personal home address of every patient
options.C: Detailed medical diagnoses of injection recipients
options.D: Daily weather conditions at the facility

explanation: Correct! The stock section is strictly about numbers: what we started with, what we used, and what is left. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why is signing off at the very end of the monitoring form compulsory?

options.A: It proves that the nursing supervisor worked overtime hours
options.B: It allows the central store to bill individual patients directly
options.C: It serves as a legal waiver for expired medical supplies
options.D: It establishes accountability for the accuracy of the reported data

explanation: You nailed it. A signature means someone is taking responsibility to verify that the numbers written down are actually correct. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: When is the best time to record numbers for your monthly injection safety report?

options.A: On a daily basis in the ward logbook
options.B: Whenever a patient makes a formal complaint
options.C: From memory at the very end of the year
options.D: Only when an inspector visits the clinic

explanation: Exactly! Jotting things down daily saves you from guessing games at month-end and keeps your records accurate. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the biggest risk of trying to estimate your injection usage from memory?

options.A: It automatically invalidates the nurse's practicing license
options.B: It causes immediate physical damage to safety boxes
options.C: It doubles the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: It distorts supply chain forecasts and leads to future stockouts

explanation: Spot on! If our recorded guesses are wrong, the central store will send the wrong quantity, leading to frustrating shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: What makes an auto-disable (AD) syringe special?

options.A: It locks or breaks after a single use to prevent reuse
options.B: It changes color when exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: It can be sterilized in boiling water up to ten times
options.D: It has a detachable needle that can be safely recapped

explanation: Correct! AD syringes jam or break right after the first injection so nobody can accidentally reuse them on another patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: Up to what level should you fill a safety box before closing it for disposal?

options.A: Emptied out daily regardless of level
options.B: Sealed only when the outer cardboard tears
options.C: Never filled beyond the three-quarter line
options.D: Packed completely to the very top rim

explanation: You got it! Stopping at the three-quarter mark ensures protruding needles don't accidentally prick anyone passing by. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: After calculating your paper totals for the month, what should a nurse do next?

options.A: Immediately throw away all the old daily logbooks
options.B: Order double the normal amount of safety boxes
options.C: Perform a physical count of the remaining stock in the storeroom
options.D: Send the unverified report directly to the federal ministry

explanation: Spot on! Always cross-check your paper math with what is actually sitting on the storeroom shelves. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: You check the storeroom and notice your physical syringe count doesn't match the logbook. What's the best move?

options.A: Change the logbook numbers to make them match perfectly without checking
options.B: Record the discrepancy and add a brief explanation in the remarks column
options.C: Hide the leftover syringes so nobody notices the mistake
options.D: Ignore the difference since small errors do not matter in healthcare

explanation: Exactly. Honesty is key in nursing; noting the gap allows supervisors to look into it properly instead of sweeping errors under the rug. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is a major red flag that supervisors look out for during a data audit?

options.A: Reporting zero waste while consumption numbers are very high
options.B: Having more than two nurses sign the document
options.C: Submitting the monthly report on the exact final day
options.D: Using blue ink instead of black ink on the monitoring form

explanation: Spot on! In a busy clinic, zero waste is almost impossible. It usually means the numbers were guessed or made up. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is retraining better than punishing staff when errors pop up in data collection?

options.A: Staff members prefer being disciplined over learning new skills
options.B: Retraining is always cheaper than buying new paper forms
options.C: Punitive measures violate international supply chain laws
options.D: Punishment encourages staff to hide mistakes rather than fix them

explanation: You got it! When people are terrified of punishment, they fake records to look flawless, which ruins the reliability of our health data. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: Where does a primary health clinic in Nigeria send its monthly injection safety report first?

options.A: The Local Government Area (LGA) focal officer
options.D: Directly to the Federal Minister of Health

explanation: Correct! Reports start locally at the LGA level before moving upward to the state and federal tables. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why do we follow a step-by-step reporting ladder for injection safety data?

options.A: It allows individual nurses to bypass hospital management
options.B: It prevents state and federal officers from seeing local clinic errors
options.C: It ensures that paperwork stays inside the hospital indefinitely
options.D: It allows data to be properly aggregated for national procurement planning

explanation: Spot on! Gathering data upward gives the country the accurate totals it needs to buy and distribute supplies for everyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h8)
